subject: Redwood Private / VPC pricing discovery - FinTechCo
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@fintechco.com>, John Miller <jmiller@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 15:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Private / VPC pricing discovery - FinTechCo

Hi Alice / John —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the items we promised to follow up on: 

Summary of needs (correct me if I missed anything):
- Private/VPC deployment with customer-managed networking (VPC peering or private link)
- Environments: prod + staging at minimum; likely a dev environment as well (3 total)
- Expected steady-state token volume: ~300M tokens/month (inference only) with monthly peak activity up to ~1.2B tokens (Q4 forecast)
- Mix: ~85% text generation, ~15% embeddings/reranking; average sequence length ~400 tokens for generation bursts
- Compliance: SOC 2 in-scope, customer-managed KMS, audit logs retention 13 months
- Desired support: Enterprise (24/7 on-call, priority engineering escalation)
- Procurement: will need a formal quote/SOW and line items per environment and support tier

Action items I said I would send:
1) Baseline pricing sheet for Redwood Private (attached) — covers licensing + committed token blocks + overage rates
2) Draft mutual action plan to align milestones for security review, pilot, and go-live (attached)
3) Short note on support tiers and what’s included

A couple of qualification questions so we can get you a tighter number:
- Can you confirm whether the 1.2B tokens peak is a single-month burst or multiple months per year?
- Do you expect embeddings to scale proportionally (i.e., will the 15% share hold at peak)?
- Is the target $/1M-tokens you mentioned on the call a committed-price target or an effective blended target including overages?

I'll outline 2 pricing options in a follow-up (annual committed + per-environment license, and a lighter pilot option). If you want, we can lock a 30–45 min follow-up with Marissa to walk line items.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_private_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf (PDF, 120KB)], [Attachment: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)]

Thanks —
Ben Carter

ben@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alice Zhang <alice@fintechco.com>

Cc: John Miller <jmiller@fintechco.com>, procurement@fintechco.com
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Private / VPC pricing discovery - FinTechCo

Ben — thanks for the recap and the attachments. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Peak volume: the 1.2B tokens is expected to be a single-month burst tied to a marketing campaign in Q4; typical peak months in 2026 will be 2–3x baseline, so plan for bursts but not sustained year-round.
- Embeddings: likely to grow faster over time as we shard user profiles — for Q4 plan assume embeddings could approach 25% of total token volume during peak.
- Target economics: procurement is looking for a committed/guaranteed price target < $2,500 per 1M tokens for committed blocks. That is our negotiation target for the contracted committed volume. Overage rates can be higher but we want a committed baseline that meets that target.
- Environments: Confirming we want 3 environments (prod/staging/dev) at launch.
- Support: we need Enterprise support (24/7, security SLAs, dedicated TAM). Can you provide a line-item for Enterprise vs Premium vs Standard in the quote?

Procurement has asked for: a formal quote with line items for
1) Annual platform/license fee (if applicable)
2) Committed token blocks and committed unit price per 1M tokens
3) Overage pricing per 1M tokens (for bursts)
4) Per-environment add-on (if you price environments separately)
5) Support tier cost (annual)

Happy to jump on a short call next week to review.
\Thanks,
Alice
Head of Product — ML Systems | FinTechCo
alice@fintechco.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@fintechco.com>, John Miller <jmiller@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, procurement@fintechco.com
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Private / VPC pricing discovery - FinTechCo

Alice / John —

Appreciate the clarity — that helps a lot. Below is a concise set of options built off the numbers you shared. These are ballpark commercial ranges we can firm up in a formal quote/SOW and are intended to show unit economics for your procurement team.

Option A — Annual committed (recommended for predictability)
- Annual platform/license fee: $120,000 (covers control plane, management, KMS integrations, audit logs)
- Environments: pricing assumes 3 environments included in the license (prod/stage/dev). Additional environments: $18,000/env/year
- Committed token block: 360M tokens/month (4.32B tokens/year) — unit price: $2,100 per 1M tokens (committed)
- Overage (burst) rate: $2,900 per 1M tokens (applies to tokens beyond committed monthly allocation)
- Support: Enterprise Support add-on: $75,000/year (24/7, dedicated TAM, 4-hr incident SLA). Premium (business hours + priority) $30,000/year. Standard included with license.

Option B — Pilot / limited commit (shorter term)
- One-year pilot: $45,000 platform fee (reduced)
- Committed block: 150M tokens/month — unit price: $2,400 per 1M tokens
- Overage: $3,200 per 1M tokens
- Environments: pilot includes prod + staging (2 envs); third dev env available at $12,000/year

Notes on unit economics:
- With Option A and your Q4 burst profile (assuming 1.2B tokens in the peak month), effective blended cost for that month would be calculated against the committed allocation + overage. We can model an annual blended $/1M for procurement if you share expected month-by-month profile.
- For your stated procurement target (< $2,500 per 1M tokens committed), Option A at $2,100 meets that target for committed blocks. 

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll create a line-item quote (license, environments, committed token tiers, overage, support) and share a draft SOW by EOD tomorrow.
- If procurement wants, Marissa can run a short technical checklist for network/KMS requirements to include in the SOW.
- Schedule a 30-min commercial review with procurement + engineering next week to finalize structure. Does Wed or Thu afternoon (PDT) work?

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_support_matrix.pdf (PDF, 80KB)]

Ben Carter
